state:
Advise on a delivery sequence for Can's build and package architecture, as a design proposal only. The project's priorities are explicit ownership, simplicity, reproducible complete workflows and economical authoring; evaluate all alternatives against these same outcomes.
Verified repository evidence: package.json pins bun@1.4.2 and workspaces packages/*, with 13 TypeScript package manifests. Its build manually orders values, contracts, work-kernel, identity, ui, interfaces, then tsc state/stdlib/testkit/cloudflare and CLI chmod. A production AST scan of literal import/export declarations found 165 relative cross-package edges in 115 non-test src files, 163 pointing to contracts source. It excludes test and dynamic-import coverage. Some actual consumers in services/files/state/ui/values/work lack corresponding manifest dependencies, and broad TypeScript roots plus imports pull sibling source into compilation. Explicit ../../contracts/src includes in values/state actually resolve to nonexistent root paths. A cloudflare dynamic loader reads state/dist internals without a state dependency; runtime identity is only a devDependency. A state work-loader has a computed TS-source dev/checkout fallback reached by cloudflare invocation, while work already has a type-only state command edge: blindly recording both directions creates a cycle and may require a shared contract or injected API seam. Rust includes a standalone compiler CLI Cargo.toml, a private values workspace containing semantics/bindings, a work-kernel Cargo.toml, cloudflare/preparation process CLI Cargo.toml and loader-smoke tests. Python tools are standard-library scripts/tests without pyproject or uv workspace. No Go code, go.mod or go.work was found; Go is an intended future part of the mix. Values bindings are opt-in WASM and work-kernel has build:wasm; preserve current backend defaults.
Verified official evidence as of 2026-10-06: https://turborepo.dev/blog/2-11 (2026-09-18) documents native Cargo, uv and go.work workspace discovery and one mixed-language task graph, explicitly experimental and subject to change. https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/boundaries documents an experimental boundary check for outside-package imports and undeclared dependencies. https://bun.sh/docs/pm/workspaces supports workspace:* internal dependencies. None proves this repository's nested/standalone workspace discovery, cache/toolchain key correctness, WASM artifact restoration or test/dynamic-load coverage.
Every option repairs the same boundary policy: TypeScript consumers declare dependencies using workspace:*; imports cross packages only through exported public package entrypoints, never sibling src/dist paths or alias bypasses. Validation must include tests and dynamic loads. Native dependency ownership remains in Cargo/go/pyproject declarations; do not require gratuitous package.json wrappers for every native package. Optional task adapters do not replace native dependency declarations. These are alternatives for the first delivery stage, not differing final quality bars.
A repairs these boundaries while retaining Bun and manual orchestration initially. It minimizes simultaneous change and new infrastructure but retains maintenance of explicit build ordering and postpones shared cache/affected scheduling.
B repairs boundaries and adds Turbo orchestration through existing package.json task scripts, using deliberate adapters for native/tool tasks initially. It offers dependency scheduling and caching using a conventional JS task layer but requires explicit cross-toolchain edges and adapter/cache-input maintenance; it does not mean each native crate must acquire an npm identity.
C repairs boundaries and adds Turbo with experimental native discovery initially, verifying mixed nested-workspace, toolchain and artifact behavior before cutover. It can derive more task/dependency information from native owners and avoid adapter duplication, while adding experimental compatibility and discovery/configuration validation work. A failed validation keeps the existing path until resolved.
No repository-specific clean-build/cache benchmark or native discovery proof is available. Do not equate importing relative source with a fixed graph by merely adding Turbo. Prefer unresolved if evidence cannot justify any sequence.

delivery_sequence.instructions: Which initial delivery sequence best fits the stated ownership, simplicity and reproducibility goals, considering equivalent boundary repair and the verified implementation evidence?

criteria.A: Repair boundaries first and retain the existing Bun/manual build at this stage, balancing limited migration scope against continued ordering maintenance.
criteria.B: Repair boundaries and introduce Turbo via existing JS task declarations with selective native/tool adapters, balancing scheduling/cache benefits against adapter and input upkeep.
criteria.C: Repair boundaries and adopt native Turbo discovery after verifying the experimental mixed-language path, balancing native declaration reuse against compatibility and validation effort.
criteria.unresolved: The evidence cannot distinguish the delivery choices responsibly; obtain targeted proof before selecting one.
